en: Regarding keeping a cat in the property, I am willing to pay a pet bond and cover the cost of any damage.
alt: If I'm allowed a cat in the property, I'm happy to pay a pet bond and to pay for any damage it causes.
point: ‘关于…一事’ = Regarding + -ing

zh: 我家猫的手术费用，请直接向我的宠物保险公司开发票。
en: Could you please invoice my pet insurer directly for the cost of my cat's surgery?
alt: Please send the invoice for my cat's operation straight to my pet insurance company.
point: 话题‘手术费用’ 用 invoice … for 放到后面

zh: 昨天开会时我发了脾气，对此我深表歉意。
en: I would like to sincerely apologise for losing my temper in yesterday's meeting with the team.
alt: Please accept my sincere apologies for my outburst at yesterday's team meeting.
point: ‘对此…歉意’ 话题放到 apologise for 后面

zh: 您的反馈我们非常重视，提到的问题会在下周的会议上讨论。
en: We take your feedback very seriously, and we will discuss the issues you raised at next week's meeting.
alt: Your feedback is important to us, and the concerns you raised will be on the agenda next week.
point: 话题‘反馈’放回 take 后；重视 = take seriously

zh: 这段时间的压力我已经向主管反映了，希望能调整一下工作量。
en: I have raised the pressure I've been under with my manager and asked whether my workload could be adjusted.
alt: I've spoken to my manager about how stretched I've been and asked for my workload to be reviewed.
point: 话题‘压力’ 用 raise … with；反映 = raise

zh: 这个项目我不是不想接，只是手上的活已经排满了，要不先放一放，下个月再说？
en: It's not that I don't want to take this project on, it's just that my plate's pretty full at the moment. Could we put it on the back burner until next month?
alt: I'd genuinely like to pick this project up, but I'm stretched thin right now — could it wait until next month?
point: 话题放回 take on 后；放一放 = put on the back burner

zh: 客户那边我来搞定，内部的问题就靠你们了，别到时候又互相推来推去。
en: I'll smooth things over with the client, but the internal stuff is down to you lot, and let's not end up passing the buck again.
alt: Leave the client to me; the internal side is yours to sort, and no finger-pointing this time.
point: 话题‘客户那边’ 用 smooth things over with；互相推 = pass the buck

zh: 老板的意思我大概听明白了，嘴上说不急，其实下周一之前就想看到东西。
en: I think I've got the gist of what the boss means — he says there's no rush, but really he wants something on his desk by Monday.
alt: Reading between the lines, the boss says it's not urgent but actually expects to see something by Monday.
point: 话题‘老板的意思’ = what the boss means；大概明白 = get the gist

zh: 那个系统说实话我是不太想碰，代码乱成一团，谁动谁背锅。
en: To be honest, that system's one I'd rather keep well away from. The code's a total mess, and whoever touches it ends up carrying the can.
alt: Frankly, I'd rather not go near that system — the code's spaghetti and anyone who changes it gets the blame.
point: 话题‘那个系统’ 用 one I'd rather keep away from；背锅 = carry the can

zh: 新版本的事你先别跟用户打包票，测试那边还在冒问题，到时候兑现不了就尴尬了。
en: I'd hold off on promising users anything about the new release, because testing's still turning up issues and it'd be awkward if we couldn't deliver.
alt: Maybe don't commit to anything on the new release just yet — testing keeps finding problems and we don't want egg on our faces.
point: 话题‘新版本的事’ 用 promise … about；先别 = hold off on

zh: 密码管理器我劝了他半天，他就是不肯用，密码还是贴在便利贴上。
en: I spent ages trying to talk him into using a password manager, but he's having none of it — his passwords are still on sticky notes.
alt: I've tried everything to get him onto a password manager, but he won't budge, so it's still sticky notes on the monitor.
point: 话题放进 talk him into using；就是不肯 = having none of it

zh: 薪资这块我暂时不想把话说死，我更看重整体待遇，比如灵活办公和培训机会。
en: I don't want to pin myself down on salary just yet. I'm more interested in the overall package, things like flexible working and training opportunities.
alt: I'd rather not commit to a number yet — the whole package matters more to me, including flexibility and development.
point: 话题‘薪资这块’ 用 pin myself down on；不把话说死

zh: 那家公司的 offer 纸面上看是不错，可我总觉得哪里不对劲，面试官连团队情况都含糊其辞。
en: On paper their offer looks great, but something doesn't quite add up. The interviewer was pretty vague about the team, which set alarm bells ringing.
alt: Their offer ticks all the boxes on paper, yet I've got a funny feeling about it — they were so cagey about the team.
point: 话题‘offer’ 用 on paper；不对劲 = doesn't add up

zh: 推荐人的事想请你帮个忙，不过你要是觉得不方便，千万别勉强。
en: I was wondering if you'd be happy to be one of my referees, but honestly, if it's not a good time, please don't feel obliged.
alt: Would you be willing to act as a referee for me? No pressure at all if it's awkward for you.
point: 话题‘推荐人的事’ 用 be my referee；别勉强 = don't feel obliged

zh: 这门统计课我不是学不会，就是一看到公式脑子就转不动了。
en: It's not that I can't get my head around this stats paper, it's just that my brain seizes up the moment I see a formula.
alt: I can follow the stats course in theory, but as soon as a formula appears my mind goes blank.
point: 话题‘统计课’ 用 get my head around；脑子转不动 = seize up

zh: 论文的结构按你说的改也行，不过我觉得第二部分有点喧宾夺主了。
en: Restructuring the essay the way you've suggested could work, though I wonder if the second section ends up stealing the show a bit.
alt: Your restructure could work, but I'm not sure the second section should take over quite so much.
point: 话题‘结构’ 变成 Restructuring … 作主语；喧宾夺主 = steal the show

zh: 小组作业的分工我就直说了，上次大部分活都是我干的，这次得平均一点。
en: I'll be upfront about splitting the group work: I ended up doing the lion's share last time, so this time it needs to be a bit more even.
alt: Can I be honest about who does what? I carried most of the load last time, so I'd like a fairer split this round.
point: 话题‘分工’ 用 be upfront about；大部分 = the lion's share

zh: 洗碗这事我不是在抱怨谁，只是好像每次都落到我头上。
en: I'm not having a go at anyone about the dishes, it's just that they always seem to end up landing on my plate.
alt: I'm not pointing fingers, but somehow the washing-up always ends up being my job.
point: 话题‘洗碗这事’ 用 about the dishes；落到我头上 = land on my plate

zh: 这张旧沙发你要是舍不得扔，至少把它挪到车库去，客厅都快转不开身了。
en: If you can't bear to part with this old couch, could we at least shift it into the garage? There's barely room to swing a cat in the lounge.
alt: I know you're attached to the old couch, but can it live in the garage? The lounge is so cramped.
point: 把…挪到车库 = shift it into the garage；舍不得扔 = can't part with

zh: 装修的事我们先别急着拍板，把预算理清楚再说，免得到时候骑虎难下。
en: Let's not rush into a decision on the renovations. We should get the budget straight first, so we don't end up in over our heads.
alt: Before we commit to the reno, let's nail down the budget so we don't get halfway and find we can't afford to finish.
point: 话题‘装修的事’ 用 a decision on；骑虎难下 = in over our heads

zh: 押金的事我也不想闹到仲裁庭，要是您能退一部分，这事我们就算翻篇了。
en: I'd really rather not take the bond issue to the Tenancy Tribunal. If you could refund part of it, I'm happy to draw a line under it.
alt: Neither of us wants the hassle of the Tribunal over the bond, so if you return some of it, I'll consider the matter closed.
point: 话题‘押金的事’ 用 take … to；翻篇 = draw a line under it

zh: 这房子的位置是没得说，不过丑话说在前头，冬天潮得厉害。
en: You can't beat this place for location, but I should be upfront with you: it gets seriously damp in winter.
alt: The location's second to none, though I'd be lying if I said it didn't get damp in winter.
point: 话题‘位置’ 用 can't beat … for；丑话说在前头 = be upfront

zh: 房东那边还是我去说吧，他对你有点成见，我出面可能好谈一些。
en: Let me have a word with the landlord. He's got a bit of a thing against you, so it might go down better coming from me.
alt: I'll talk to the landlord — he seems to have it in for you a bit, so it may land better if I raise it.
point: 话题‘房东那边’ 放到 have a word with 后；有成见 = have a thing against

zh: 停车的事我想跟他好好说，没必要搞得两家都下不来台，更别说结下梁子了。
en: I'd like to raise the parking thing with him nicely. There's no need to put either of us on the spot, let alone start a feud.
alt: I'll bring up the parking gently — no point embarrassing anyone or starting a war over the street.
point: 话题‘停车的事’ 用 raise … with；结梁子 = start a feud

zh: 他们家的狗叫我们也就忍了，可凌晨三点还在叫，这就有点说不过去了。
en: We've learnt to live with their dog barking, but carrying on at three in the morning is a bit much, to be honest.
alt: We've put up with the barking so far, but three a.m. is pushing it.
point: 话题‘狗叫’ 放到 live with 后；说不过去 = a bit much

zh: 社区花园的提议我原则上支持，不过谁来浇水除草，这个得先说清楚再动手。
en: I'm all for the community garden in principle, but we'd need to sort out who's actually doing the watering and weeding before we get stuck in.
alt: In theory I love the idea of a community garden, but let's agree who's on watering and weeding duty first.
point: 话题‘提议’ 用 all for；动手 = get stuck in

zh: 这家电力公司我是彻底受够了，账单每次都对不上，打电话又永远在排队。
en: I've well and truly had it with this power company. The bills never add up, and whenever I ring them I'm stuck on hold forever.
alt: I'm completely fed up with this power company — dodgy bills every month and endless hold music.
point: 话题‘这家公司’ 用 had it with；受够了

zh: 提前解约要交钱这事，签约时他们一个字都没提，现在倒好，想走先交钱。
en: They never breathed a word about an early exit fee when I signed up, and now, funnily enough, I can't leave without paying one.
alt: Nobody mentioned a break fee when I signed, yet suddenly I have to pay to get out of the contract.
point: 话题‘违约金’ 用 breathe a word about；现在倒好 = funnily enough

zh: 网速慢这个问题你跟他们说也没用，他们只会让你重启路由器，然后就没下文了。
en: There's no point raising the slow internet with them. They'll just tell you to restart the router, and then you'll never hear another thing.
alt: Complaining about the speed gets you nowhere — it's 'have you tried turning it off and on again?' and then silence.
point: 话题‘网速慢’ 用 raise … with；没下文 = never hear another thing

zh: 这个报价说实话有点离谱，不是不信任你，只是想多问几家，心里有个底。
en: To be honest, this quote's a bit steep. It's not that I don't trust you, I'd just like to get a couple more so I've got a ballpark.
alt: I'll be straight with you, the quote's on the high side — nothing personal, I just want to compare a few before deciding.
point: 话题‘报价’ 作主语说 steep；心里有个底 = get a ballpark

zh: 漏水的地方他修了三次都没修好，我看这次得换个人了。
en: He's had three goes at fixing the leak and it's still dripping, so I reckon it's time we got someone else in.
alt: Three attempts and the leak's still there — I think we need a different plumber.
point: 话题‘漏水的地方’放回 fixing 后；修三次 = have three goes at

zh: 这种小活我自己就能对付，真请人来，光上门费都够我买一套新工具了。
en: I can handle little jobs like this myself. If I got a tradie in, the call-out fee alone would pay for a whole new set of tools.
alt: Small jobs like this I can do myself — a tradesperson's call-out charge would cost more than a new toolkit.
point: 话题‘这种小活’放回 handle 后；上门费 = call-out fee

zh: 这件外套我是挺喜欢的，可这个价我得再想想，以我的运气，一买它准打折。
en: I do love this coat, but I'd want to sleep on it at that price — knowing my luck, it'd go on sale the day after I bought it.
alt: I'm really tempted by this coat, but not at full price; with my luck it'll be half off next week.
point: 话题放回 love 后，用 do 加强；再想想 = sleep on it

zh: 退货的事我跟店员磨了半天，她最后才不情不愿地同意给我换。
en: I went back and forth with the shop assistant over the return for ages before she grudgingly agreed to swap it.
alt: It took a lot of persuading, but the shop assistant finally, reluctantly, let me exchange it.
point: 话题‘退货的事’ 用 over the return；磨了半天 = go back and forth

zh: 网上买衣服我是再也不干了，十件里八件尺码不对，退来退去太折腾。
en: I've sworn off buying clothes online. Eight times out of ten the size is wrong, and sending stuff back is more hassle than it's worth.
alt: I've given up on online clothes shopping — the sizing's always off and returns are a nightmare.
point: 话题‘网上买衣服’ 用 swear off -ing；太折腾 = more hassle than it's worth

zh: 这家店的菜倒是挑不出毛病，就是服务有待提高，上菜慢不说，态度也一般。
en: I can't really fault the food here, but the service could do with some work. Not only is it slow, the staff aren't exactly friendly either.
alt: The food's spot on; the service, on the other hand, is slow and a bit offhand.
point: 话题‘菜’ 用 can't fault；有待提高 = could do with some work

zh: 这次的账单我们就各付各的，你别跟我抢，上次已经是你请的了。
en: Let's just split the bill this time, and don't even think about fighting me for it, because you shouted last time.
alt: We're going halves today, no arguments — you paid last time.
point: 话题‘账单’放回 split 后；请客 = shout

zh: 那家新开的餐厅我听说口碑两极分化，要不先去吃个午饭试试，别一下就订年会晚宴。
en: I've heard that new place is a bit hit and miss, so maybe we should try it for lunch first rather than booking it for the end-of-year do.
alt: Reviews of the new restaurant are mixed, so let's test it out over lunch before we commit to it for the work party.
point: 话题‘那家餐厅’ 用 try it for；两极分化 = hit and miss

zh: 借钱这事吧，不是我不想帮，只是上次借出去的到现在都还没还回来。
en: When it comes to lending money, it's not that I don't want to help, it's just that I'm still waiting to get back what I lent last time.
alt: As far as lending goes, I'd like to help, but I haven't been paid back from last time yet.
point: 话题‘借钱这事’ = When it comes to lending money

zh: 投资的事我是外行，你最好找个正经的理财顾问聊聊，别听网上那些人瞎说。
en: I'm no expert when it comes to investing, so you'd be better off talking to a proper financial adviser than listening to randoms online.
alt: Investing's not really my area — I'd see a qualified adviser rather than trusting whatever people post online.
point: 话题‘投资的事’ 用 when it comes to；外行 = no expert

zh: 买房的首付我们攒得差不多了，就是利率一直这样，心里还是有点没底。
en: We've just about scraped together the deposit for a house, but with interest rates the way they are, we're a bit nervous about taking the plunge.
alt: We're nearly there with the house deposit, though the interest rates are making us think twice about jumping in.
point: 话题‘首付’放回 scrape together 后；下决心买 = take the plunge

zh: 签证的事你别太焦虑，材料都交齐了，剩下的就只能等，急也没用。
en: Try not to stress about the visa. All your paperwork's in, so it's really just a waiting game now, and worrying won't speed it up.
alt: Don't lose sleep over the visa — everything's submitted, and fretting won't make it come any faster.
point: 话题‘签证的事’ 用 stress about；只能等 = a waiting game

zh: 这张表我填了三遍都被退回来了，我真怀疑他们是不是故意刁难人。
en: This form's been sent back to me three times now. I'm starting to wonder if they're deliberately making life difficult.
alt: Three times they've returned this form — I'm beginning to think they're being awkward on purpose.
point: 话题‘这张表’ 作主语用被动 sent back；刁难 = make life difficult

zh: 市政那边我打过电话了，对方说会“研究研究”，你懂的，基本就是没戏。
en: I've already rung the council, and they said they'd 'look into it', which, as we all know, is code for 'don't hold your breath'.
alt: I called the council and got the usual 'we'll look into it', so I wouldn't get your hopes up.
point: 话题‘市政那边’ 用 ring the council；没戏 = don't hold your breath

zh: 化验单上那几项指标，医生说不用太紧张，不过最好还是把酒戒了。
en: The GP said I shouldn't read too much into those numbers on my results, but that cutting out alcohol wouldn't be a bad idea.
alt: According to my doctor, those test results aren't a big worry, though giving up the booze would be sensible.
point: 话题‘指标’ 用 read too much into；把酒戒了 = cut out alcohol

zh: 这颗牙我本来想拖到年底再去看，结果昨晚疼得我一宿没睡。
en: I'd been planning to put off seeing the dentist about this tooth until the end of the year, but it kept me up all night.
alt: I was going to leave this tooth till the end of the year, but last night the pain had other ideas.
point: 话题‘这颗牙’ 用 about this tooth；拖 = put off

zh: 心理咨询这件事我犹豫了很久，后来想想，与其一个人硬扛，不如找个人聊聊。
en: I sat on the fence about seeing a counsellor for ages, but eventually I figured talking to someone beats trying to tough it out on my own.
alt: I dithered for a long time about counselling, but in the end it made more sense than gritting my teeth alone.
point: 话题‘心理咨询’ 用 about seeing a counsellor；硬扛 = tough it out

zh: 那次地震我们家倒没什么损失，就是东西被摇得乱七八糟，到现在还没收拾完。
en: We got off pretty lightly in the earthquake, really. Nothing broke, everything just got thrown all over the place, and we still haven't finished putting it back.
alt: The quake didn't do us much harm, but the house was turned upside down and we're still tidying up.
point: 话题‘那次地震’ 用 got off lightly in；收拾 = put back

zh: 报警这事先别急，我们先确认是不是真丢了，说不定是落在你朋友车上了。
en: Let's hold off on calling the police for now and make sure it's actually gone first. It might just have been left in your friend's car.
alt: Before we ring the police, let's double-check it's really missing — it could easily be sitting in your mate's car.
point: 话题‘报警这事’ 用 hold off on -ing

zh: 保险那些事我们回头再慢慢弄，眼下最要紧的是大家都没受伤。
en: We can sort out the insurance side of things later. Right now, the main thing is that nobody got hurt, and that's what counts.
alt: The insurance can wait — what really matters is that everyone's safe.
point: 话题‘保险那些事’ = the insurance side of things

zh: 这辆二手车我看着挺好，不过买之前还是找个技师从头到尾查一遍，免得踩坑。
en: This second-hand car looks great to me, but I'd still get a mechanic to give it the once-over before buying, just so we don't get stung.
alt: The used car seems fine, but let's have a mechanic check it out before we hand over any money.
point: 话题‘这辆车’ 放进 give it the once-over；踩坑 = get stung

zh: 开车这件事我是真没天赋，路考考了三次才过，现在倒车入库还是心慌。
en: Driving just isn't my strong point. It took me three goes to pass my test, and reverse parking still sets my nerves on edge.
alt: I'm not a natural behind the wheel — I failed my test twice, and reversing into a park still makes me sweat.
point: 话题‘开车这件事’ 作主语：isn't my strong point

zh: 早高峰的路况你就别指望了，与其开车堵着，还不如坐火车，起码能看会儿书。
en: Don't count on the roads being clear at rush hour. Rather than sitting in traffic, you're better off getting the train, where at least you can read.
alt: Forget about a quick drive at peak time — the train beats being stuck in traffic, and you can read on the way.
point: 话题‘路况’ 用 count on … being clear

zh: 这次的行程我觉得排得有点满，要不砍掉一两个景点，留点时间放松？
en: I feel like we've crammed a bit too much into this trip. How about we ditch a couple of the sights and leave ourselves some breathing room?
alt: The itinerary's looking a bit packed — maybe we could drop one or two stops and give ourselves time to relax?
point: 话题‘行程’ 用 cram too much into；砍掉 = ditch

zh: 旅行保险这东西平时觉得多余，真出了事你就知道它的好了。
en: Travel insurance always feels like money down the drain until something goes wrong, and then you're very glad you've got it.
alt: You never think you need travel insurance until you do, and then it's worth every cent.
point: 话题‘旅行保险’ 作主语；多余 = money down the drain

zh: 住的地方你来挑吧，我不讲究，只要干净、离车站近，别的都好说。
en: I'll leave the accommodation up to you. I'm not fussy, so as long as it's clean and handy to the station, I'm easy.
alt: You choose where we stay — I'm not picky, just somewhere clean and close to the station.
point: 话题‘住的地方’ 用 leave … up to you；都好说 = I'm easy

zh: 那条线路我劝你冬天还是别去，天气说变就变，就算老手也在那儿栽过跟头。
en: I wouldn't tackle that track in winter if I were you. The weather can turn in an instant, and even experienced trampers have come unstuck there.
alt: I'd save that track for summer — the weather changes fast up there and it's caught out plenty of seasoned trampers.
point: 话题‘那条线路’放回 tackle 后；栽跟头 = come unstuck

zh: 钓鱼我是一窍不通，不过你们要是缺个人看冰箱、递啤酒，我倒是可以凑个数。
en: I don't know the first thing about fishing, but if you need someone to look after the chilly bin and hand out the beers, count me in.
alt: Fishing's not my thing at all, but I'm happy to come along as chief chilly bin minder.
point: 话题‘钓鱼’ 用 know the first thing about；凑个数 = count me in

zh: 防晒这件事在这儿可真不能马虎，上次我只抹了一回，结果晒得跟只龙虾似的。
en: Don't be slack about sunscreen here. Last time I only put it on once, and I ended up looking like a boiled lobster by the afternoon.
alt: Take the sunblock seriously here — I skimped on it last time and went as red as a lobster.
point: 话题‘防晒’ 用 slack about；晒伤 = look like a lobster

zh: 比赛结果我倒是无所谓，主要是想跟大家出来活动活动，完了顺便喝一杯。
en: I'm not too fussed about the result, to be honest. It's more about getting out with the team and grabbing a drink together afterwards.
alt: Winning or losing doesn't bother me much; I'm mainly there for the exercise and the beer afterwards.
point: 话题‘比赛结果’ 用 fussed about；无所谓

zh: 教练的战术我不好多说什么，但都连输五场了，总得有人站出来说句话吧。
en: It's not really my place to question the coach's tactics, but after five losses on the trot, surely someone's got to speak up?
alt: I don't want to second-guess the coach, but five defeats in a row means someone has to say something.
point: 话题‘战术’放到 question 后；连输 = on the trot

zh: 马拉松是我一时冲动报的名，现在想想，可能有点不自量力了。
en: I signed up for the marathon on a bit of a whim, and now I'm wondering if I've bitten off more than I can chew.
alt: Entering the marathon was a spur-of-the-moment thing, and I'm starting to think I've overdone it.
point: 话题‘马拉松’放到 sign up for 后；不自量力 = bite off more than I can chew

zh: 那部电影大家都说好，我看了倒觉得一般，可能是期望太高了吧。
en: Everyone raved about that film, but it didn't really live up to the hype for me. Maybe my expectations were just too high.
alt: People couldn't stop talking about that movie, yet I came away a bit underwhelmed — probably expected too much.
point: 话题‘那部电影’ 用 rave about；一般 = not live up to the hype

zh: 合唱团我是真想去，就是周三晚上实在抽不出空，要不明年再看吧。
en: I'd love to join the choir, I really would, but Wednesday nights are a write-off for me. Maybe I'll revisit it next year.
alt: Joining the choir really appeals, but Wednesdays are impossible for me at the moment — perhaps next year.
point: 话题‘合唱团’放回 join 后；抽不出空 = a write-off

zh: 这次的发型我不太满意，不过剪都剪了，反正过几个星期就长回来了。
en: I'm not exactly over the moon with this haircut, but there's no undoing it now, and it'll grow out in a few weeks anyway.
alt: This haircut isn't my favourite, but it's done now, and give it a few weeks and nobody will notice.
point: 话题‘发型’ 用 over the moon with；剪都剪了 = no undoing it

zh: 这周末的聚会我就不去了，不是不给面子，实在累得不行，只想在家躺着。
en: I think I'll give the party a miss this weekend. It's nothing personal, I'm just completely knackered and need a night in.
alt: I'm going to sit this weekend's party out — not because of anything you've done, I'm just shattered.
point: 话题‘聚会’ 用 give … a miss；不是不给面子 = nothing personal

zh: 他那个人说什么你都别往心里去，就是说话直了点，其实心眼不坏。
en: Don't take anything he says personally. He can come across as very blunt, but his heart's in the right place.
alt: Try not to let his comments get to you — he's direct to a fault, but he means well.
point: ‘他那个人’ 变成 anything he says；心眼不坏 = heart's in the right place

zh: 聊天的话题你放心，政治和房价我是绝对不碰的，天气和橄榄球总归是安全的。
en: Don't worry about the small talk. I'll stay well away from politics and house prices, because the weather and rugby are always safe bets.
alt: Relax, I won't bring up politics or the housing market — I'll stick to safe ground like the weather and the rugby.
point: 话题‘聊天的话题’ = the small talk；安全牌 = a safe bet

zh: 婚礼的预算我们说好了最多两万，结果光场地就花掉了一半。
en: We agreed to keep the wedding to twenty grand, tops, and the venue alone has already eaten up half of it.
alt: Our wedding budget was meant to be twenty thousand max, but the venue's swallowed half of that already.
point: 话题‘预算’ 用 keep … to；花掉 = eat up

zh: 过年回不回国这事，我爸妈嘴上说随我，其实心里巴不得我回去。
en: As for whether I go home for Chinese New Year, my parents say it's up to me, but I know they're secretly dying for me to come.
alt: My parents insist it's my call whether I fly home for New Year, but deep down they're desperate for me to be there.
point: 话题‘这事’ = As for whether …；巴不得 = dying for

zh: 送礼这件事真让我头疼，送贵了怕对方有压力，送便宜了又显得没诚意。
en: Gift-giving really does my head in. Spend too much and they feel awkward, spend too little and it looks like you couldn't be bothered.
alt: Choosing presents stresses me out: too pricey and it's uncomfortable, too cheap and it looks thoughtless.
point: 话题‘送礼’ 作主语 does my head in

zh: 孩子上学的问题我和我先生意见不太一样，他想送私立，我觉得附近的公立学校就挺好。
en: My husband and I don't quite see eye to eye on the kids' schooling. He's keen on private, whereas I think the local school's fine.
alt: We're not on the same page about where the kids go to school — he wants private, I'm happy with the local one.
point: 话题‘上学的问题’ 用 see eye to eye on

zh: 婆婆的好意我心领了，但带孩子的方式，我们还是想按自己的来。
en: I really do appreciate my mother-in-law's help, but when it comes to raising the kids, we'd rather do things our own way.
alt: My mother-in-law means well and I'm grateful, but we'd like to bring the children up our way.
point: ‘好意’放回 appreciate 后；带孩子方面 = when it comes to raising kids

zh: 手机这事我跟儿子谈过了，周末可以多玩一会儿，平时晚上九点必须交出来。
en: I've laid down the law with my son about his phone: he gets a bit more time at weekends, but on school nights it's handed over at nine.
alt: My son and I have had the phone talk — more screen time at weekends, but it's mine at nine on school nights.
point: 话题‘手机这事’ 用 about his phone；立规矩 = lay down the law

zh: 养狗这件事我们全家争了好几个月，最后还是孩子们把我们磨赢了。
en: We went round in circles for months about getting a dog, and in the end the kids just wore us down.
alt: The dog debate dragged on for months in our house until the kids finally got their way.
point: 话题‘养狗’ 用 about getting a dog；磨 = wear down

zh: 这只猫我们原本只打算临时收养几周，结果一不小心就养了五年。
en: We only meant to foster this cat for a few weeks, but somehow, five years later, she's very much part of the family.
alt: This cat was supposed to be a short-term foster, and five years on she's well and truly ours.
point: 话题‘这只猫’放回 foster 后；一不小心 = somehow

zh: 遛狗说好了轮流来，可每次下大雨都轮到我，你说巧不巧。
en: We agreed to take turns walking the dog, but funnily enough, it always seems to be my turn whenever it's bucketing down.
alt: Dog walks are meant to be shared, yet strangely it's always me who gets the pouring-rain shift.
point: 话题‘遛狗’ 用 take turns walking；下大雨 = bucketing down

zh: 那件事我早就放下了，你也别一直自责，都过去了。
en: I put all that behind me ages ago, so please don't keep beating yourself up over it. It's water under the bridge.
alt: I moved on from that a long time ago — honestly, stop blaming yourself, it's all in the past.
point: 话题‘那件事’ 用 put … behind me；都过去了 = water under the bridge

zh: 你的建议我真的听进去了，只是现在还没准备好做那么大的改变，给我点时间。
en: I have taken your advice on board, I promise. I'm just not ready to make such a big change yet, so bear with me.
alt: I really did listen to what you said — I just need a bit more time before making a change that big.
point: 话题‘建议’ 用 take … on board；给我点时间 = bear with me

zh: 他那些话我当时没反驳，不代表我认同，只是不想当着大家的面闹僵。
en: Just because I didn't push back on what he said doesn't mean I agreed. I just didn't want to sour the mood in front of everyone.
alt: My silence wasn't agreement — I simply didn't want to cause a scene in front of everyone.
point: 话题‘那些话’ 用 push back on；闹僵 = sour the mood
